detail.longDescription:
Security researchers have uncovered PolinRider, a North Korea-linked, self-propagating GitHub worm associated with a software supply chain attack affecting at least 7,609 repositories across 2,330 accounts.

The malware uses stolen developer credentials to modify existing Git commits while preserving their original authors, messages and timestamps. Malicious code is concealed using hundreds of invisible tab characters, making the changes difficult to identify during routine code reviews.

Researchers identified malicious pull requests targeting projects including AsyncAPI, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts. In the CircuitVerse case, the payload executed through GitHub Actions, resulting in 40 desktop installers being published from compromised build infrastructure. The affected installers reportedly remained available for more than a month.

PolinRider can also execute through build scripts and certain VS Code automatic task configurations. It attempts to steal credentials, spread to additional repositories and uses Ethereum blockchain transactions to discover command-and-control infrastructure.

One particularly concerning technique involves inserting malicious code into pull requests, allowing CI workflows to execute it and subsequently removing the changes. The final code may appear clean even though the build environment was already compromised.

The 7,609 identified repositories should not be interpreted as 7,609 confirmed successful malware executions.

Full technical analysis, attack chain and detection guidance:
https://thecybersecguru.com/news/polinrider-worm-github-supply-chain-attack/
